story.title: Lavish European travel by Texas’ ex-Juvenile Justice chief contributed to her exit, records show
story.summary: For three nights in June, Texas Juvenile Justice Department’s former executive director stayed at an ABBA-themed luxury boutique hotel in Stockholm, tucked inside the same building as a museum dedicated to the Swedish pop band. Shandra Carter, who had led the agency since 2022, was resting between speaking events in Europe. She’d just been hosting a training about five hours away at a psychiatric hospital in the southern part of Sweden and was heading soon to Helsinki for a presentation on effective staffing and behavioral reinforcement systems. The Backstage Hotel Stockholm averaged $900 a night, roughly three times the $293 nightly maximum that the U.S. State Department sets for federal employees traveling to that city.
